topic: A sister to FAR Out for academic and non-profit grant money: a public site, something very much like FAR Out, that helps a university researcher, a research office or a non-profit find and follow a route to grant money, with an opportunity search built in
topic_note: Daniel's first message is not preserved word for word in the session record; this is the request as the requirements note recorded it on 2026-10-04. The phrase "something very much like FAR Out" is his.
question: For a university researcher, a research office or a non-profit that wants grant money in the United States, what routes exist (research project grants, fellowships and training awards, programme and service grants, capacity and infrastructure money, from federal agencies and from foundations), what does each require, who actually decides, and what changed in 2025-26 that the official pages have not caught up with?

in: federal grant-making agencies, every field: research, health, education, arts and humanities, agriculture, environment, justice, housing, labour
private, community and corporate foundations and other private grantmakers: 65 recorded as a labelled editorial sample
four route families: research project grants; fellowships, career and training awards; programme and service grants; capacity and infrastructure
the entry routes: registration, becoming an eligible non-profit, joining as a subrecipient, approaching a foundation, general operating support, research at a non-profit that is not a university
standing: eligibility that belongs to the institution or its state (EPSCoR and IDeA lists, designated institutions, tax status)
the gates: registrations, identifiers, assurances and audits
the rules beneath every federal award: the Uniform Guidance, indirect costs, termination, and what changed or is contested in 2025-26
federal formula and pass-through programmes as far as the federal page: who receives the money and whom a non-profit applies to
out: state and local government grant programmes, and any state's own process for passing federal money on
contracts, SBIR/STTR from the firm's side, other transactions and procurement (covered by the sister guide FAR Out)
loans, loan guarantees, tax credits and benefits paid to individuals
grant-writing technique, and any recommendation of a paid database, consultant or grant writer
foundations beyond the sample of 65 (reached through the directory the site builds from IRS data, not through records)
funders outside the United States, and United States awards to foreign organisations except where an eligibility rule mentions them
post-award administration in depth (effort reporting, procurement standards, property), beyond the rules a newcomer meets before and at award
boundary.rationale: Daniel, 2026-10-04: federal plus foundations, state and local out for the first release; both academic and non-profit readers, split by the pathfinder; all four route families in depth; all fields. On 2026-10-05 he ruled that pass-through programmes stop at the state door and that the foundations stay as a labelled sample. The rest of the out-list was proposed by the builder and not objected to.

level: the applicant organisation and the person named in its application: what each must be, hold and do to enter a route; the funder: how it posts, reviews and decides

time_window.seminal: statute, regulation, court rulings and policy guides of any age that govern a route

interview.q: Which funders should the first release cover?
interview.answer: Federal plus foundations. (Chosen from the options offered; state and local money is out for the first release.)
Both academic and non-profit, split by the pathfinder. (Chosen from the options offered.)

interview.q: How deep should the first release go?
interview.answer: All four route families in depth. (Chosen from the options offered.)
All fields. (Chosen from the options offered.)
First "Taken for Granted"; on 2026-10-05: "Want to replace every instance of taken with token / As the naming convention goes, that is / Obviously not find and replace in the content"

interview.q: Three recommendations: stop pass-through programmes at the state door; list on route pages only programmes a reader can act on and let search reach the rest; keep the 65 foundations as a labelled editorial sample?
Add a question about field to the pathfinder?

interview.answer: And let's keep the primer section BUT not include the questions. and let's make that toggle on future builds as well
I guess that's in the "concepts" area? Wherever the questions get presented let's make that something to add rather than a default

interview.q: The outline of eleven sections, one claim each, shown before any prose (TOPIC-WORKFLOW T4): any change?
interview.answer: No change asked for; he answered "proceed".

carried_from_far_out: situation-first spine: a pathfinder leading into a route catalogue
gates as checklists shown on every route that needs them
no connection to any specific university or non-profit in content, examples, branding or repository
anything personal stays in the visitor's browser
still_open: funders set up by Congress that are neither agency nor foundation (PCORI, the Legal Services Corporation, the Corporation for Public Broadcasting) are kept as independent-nonprofit and counted on the federal side by the pathfinder
edge cases between families (research centres, NIH DP2 and DP5, preservation grants, NIH SuRE) stand as recorded
the label no-current-notice (82 programmes) reports an absence on the funder's page and on Grants.gov; the alternative label would be unconfirmed

sources: direct fetch of official pages (grants.gov and simpler.grants.gov, agency sites, ecfr.gov, govinfo.gov, federalregister.gov, irs.gov, court sites, foundation sites)
foundation annual returns as summarised by ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer

from each dated change to the notice, order or opinion that made it

a funder's own page, policy or filing for what it says about itself

known_gaps: 166 references remain flagged after the recheck: pages that refused a second reading (nine eCFR sections, two acf.gov pages, one pcori.org page), sources with a fact the second reading did not find, and the pages read by the status pass, which were not rechecked
1077 sources were re-read only in part, because the fetch layer cuts long pages short

five contradictions between a stored fact and the page as re-read remain open (NIH R13 institute count, NSF FY2025 MRI figure, PCORI announcement count, AmeriCorps member-support share, Guam centre totals)
OMB's proposed rewrite of 2 CFR part 200 (May 29, 2026) was read only in part: the preamble and search excerpts, not the full regulatory text
three sections of 2 CFR part 200 (200.204, 200.306, 200.344) rest on GovInfo's January 1, 2025 edition; the current eCFR would not load for them
26 programmes carry the status unconfirmed and 82 the status no-current-notice; programme status was read on one day and goes out of date quickly
eight formula-programme records say the federal agency takes no application from a non-profit where the page read names only who receives the grant; two federal pages (HUD, FEMA) say so in words
foundations: the IRS e-file field documentation and the Form 990-PF Part XIV instructions are unread, and the harvest of the filings themselves is unprobed
FY2026 enacted amounts for the Education institutional-aid lines and NSF EPSCoR were not found

five pairs of change records disagree on a date or a status (ROSES-2026 date, NEA injunction scope, NSF cap date, an OJP termination, an Education interagency agreement); Executive Order 14332 is final on five records and pending-implementation on one

hosts that refused automated reading: congress.gov, uscode.house.gov (intermittent), war.gov and defense.gov, nspires.nasaprs.com, sam.gov, research.va.gov, americorps.gov, several acf.gov pages, samhsa.gov HTML pages (its PDFs load), ed.gov (intermittent), cpb.org, smartscholarship.org, report.nih.gov, courtlistener.com
court opinions read on third-party hosts are to be re-read on court sites
